articles.headline: El sorteo de la Lotería Nacional deja 300.000 euros en Lugo, Vilalba y Becerreá
articles.subtitle: El segundo premio, el 41.270, dotado con 12.000 euros por décimo, se vendió el sábado en 25 boletos: veinte en una administración de la capital y cinco más por máquina en distintos puntos de las tres localidades.
articles.body:
El sorteo de la Lotería Nacional del sábado dejó 300.000 euros en la provincia de Lugo. El segundo premio, el número 41.270, dotado con 12.000 euros por décimo, se vendió en 25 boletos repartidos entre Lugo, Vilalba y Becerreá, según informan El Progreso y La Voz de Galicia.

Veinte de esos décimos se vendieron en una administración de la Avenida da Coruña de la capital, cuya titular, Eva María Cancela Barrio, explicó que el establecimiento permaneció cerrado el sábado y que la mayor parte de los boletos correspondían a clientes habituales que tenían reservado el número. Los otros cinco se vendieron por máquina en distintos puntos de venta de Lugo y de Becerreá.

En Vilalba, la administración de Carmen Rouco repartió otro décimo del mismo número; su establecimiento ya vendió el Gordo de Navidad en 2017. Al tratarse de un premio inferior a 40.000 euros por décimo, la cantidad está exenta de impuestos.

articles.headline: Tomás Notario Vacas, exalcalde de Lugo, celebra sus 100 años rodeado de su familia y amigos
articles.subtitle: El ingeniero, que gobernó la ciudad entre 1976 y 1977 y entre 1991 y 1995, cumplió el sábado un siglo de vida en una comida en el Gran Hotel Lugo con medio centenar de invitados.
articles.body:
Tomás Notario Vacas, exalcalde de Lugo en dos mandatos, celebró el sábado su centenario rodeado de su familia y de sus amigos. El ingeniero, nacido en 1926, reunió a medio centenar de personas en una comida en el Gran Hotel Lugo bajo el lema 'Ayer, hoy y siempre', según relata El Progreso.

Notario gobernó la ciudad entre 1976 y 1977 y entre 1991 y 1995. En su primera etapa impulsó obras como el puente nuevo sobre el Miño y, en la segunda, la circunvalación de la N-VI, la peatonalización del centro y la primera residencia de ancianos de la ciudad.

Al acto asistieron la alcaldesa, Elena Candia, el concejal de Urbanismo, Ramón Cabarcos, y la concejala María Reigosa, entre otros. Nacido en Córdoba (Argentina), Notario se instaló en Lugo en 1960. En una entrevista con El Progreso el pasado febrero recordó que fue Cacharro quien le hizo la lista para presentarse a las elecciones, y la fundación que lleva su nombre consolida sus becas de estudios, que este año celebran su quinta edición.

articles.headline: El Gobierno prepara un plan económico para revitalizar Ceuta tras la crisis migratoria
articles.subtitle: El Ejecutivo trabaja en un paquete de al menos 15 millones de euros para el comercio, con rebajas fiscales y ayudas directas, mientras el Consejo de Ministros aprobará el martes 25 millones para los menores.
articles.body:
El Gobierno prepara un plan de reactivación económica para Ceuta tras la crisis migratoria del 30 de julio. Moncloa ha pedido ideas a todos los ministerios y trabaja con cuantificaciones iniciales de al menos 15 millones de euros para el comercio de la ciudad, con rebajas de impuestos, reducción de cotizaciones a la Seguridad Social y ayudas directas para compensar el lucro cesante, según publica El País.

El vicepresidente primero, Carlos Cuerpo, tiene previsto desplazarse a la ciudad la próxima semana para perfilar el plan con los sectores afectados. El Consejo de Ministros aprobará este martes un fondo de 25 millones de euros para atender a los menores no acompañados, que servirá entre otras cosas para financiar el traslado de 500 niñas a la Península.

El Ejecutivo trabaja en tres ejes: gestión diplomática y refuerzo de seguridad, gestión humanitaria y recuperación económica. El Ayuntamiento de Ceuta, gobernado por el PP, insiste en expulsar a todos los que entraron el 30 y 31 de julio, algo que la legislación vigente hace muy difícil en el caso de los adultos e imposible en el de los menores.

articles.headline: Marruecos pide a España que devuelva a los migrantes supervivientes y fallecidos de la entrada masiva a Ceuta
articles.subtitle: El ministro de Justicia marroquí, Abdellatif Ouahbi, reclamó el sábado la repatriación de los supervivientes y de los cuerpos de los fallecidos, condicionada a informes forenses y a la devolución de los menores.
articles.body:
Marruecos pidió este sábado a España que devuelva a los migrantes supervivientes de la entrada masiva del 30 de julio a Ceuta, así como los cuerpos de los fallecidos. El ministro de Justicia marroquí, Abdellatif Ouahbi, condicionó esa repatriación a la elaboración de informes forenses y a la devolución de los menores marroquíes, y subrayó: 'Nosotros no separamos entre vivos y muertos'.

El viernes fueron enterrados en el cementerio musulmán de Ceuta los primeros 18 migrantes que murieron ahogados durante la crisis, tres semanas después de un salto en el que entraron más de 70.000 personas y en el que decenas perdieron la vida, entre ahogados y víctimas de una estampida en el espigón; el Gobierno español elevó a 67 los fallecidos a principios de agosto, según recoge la agencia AP.

El ministro marroquí insistió además en que Ceuta y Melilla constituyen un 'derecho histórico y geográfico' de Marruecos, en línea con las declaraciones que la diplomacia marroquí viene realizando desde el inicio de la crisis.

articles.headline: Estabilizado el incendio de Segorbe, que ha arrasado 630 hectáreas entre Castellón y Valencia
articles.subtitle: El fuego, originado el jueves por un rayo en la Sierra Calderona, quedó estabilizado el domingo y los vecinos de Gátova pudieron regresar a sus casas, aunque el agua aún no es potable.
articles.body:
El incendio forestal de Segorbe (Castellón) quedó estabilizado en la mañana de este domingo después de arrasar unas 630 hectáreas, 395 en el término de Segorbe y 235 en el de Gátova, con un perímetro de 18 kilómetros delimitado. La Generalitat rebajó la situación operativa del nivel 2 al 1 y la UME se retiró, según informa RTVE.

El fuego, originado el jueves por la noche por la caída de un rayo en el parque natural de la Sierra Calderona, llegó a amenazar la localidad de Gátova, cuyos vecinos fueron evacuados el viernes tras dos avisos Es-Alert. El sábado los bomberos se afanaron en impedir que las llamas alcanzaran el municipio, como relataba El País, y el domingo los vecinos pudieron regresar a sus casas a partir de las 11.00, aunque permanecen confinados para mantener despejadas las vías.

El agua de la red no es potable hasta que concluyan los análisis. En el perímetro se halló el cuerpo de un varón de 60 años, aunque las primeras pesquisas apuntan a que la muerte no está relacionada con el incendio. En la extinción participaron 130 efectivos y diez medios aéreos.

articles.headline: Detenidas diez personas tras disparar a la Guardia Civil durante la persecución de una narcolancha en Huelva
articles.subtitle: Los tripulantes de una semirrígida abrieron fuego contra una patrullera de Vigilancia Aduanera la madrugada del martes; la Guardia Civil ha desmantelado la banda e intervenido casi seis toneladas de hachís.
articles.body:
La Guardia Civil ha detenido a diez personas de una organización criminal cuyos integrantes tirotearon a una patrullera en las costas de Huelva durante una persecución en el mar. Los hechos ocurrieron durante la madrugada del lunes al martes: una embarcación del Servicio de Vigilancia Aduanera perseguía a una semirrígida cuando los tripulantes abrieron fuego contra los agentes, que respondieron e hirieron a uno de los narcos.

La patrullera sufrió una avería y tuvo que desistir, y los criminales abandonaron al herido en una playa de la costa de Cádiz, desde donde fue trasladado al hospital de Puerto Real. Este jueves, la Guardia Civil abordó la narcolancha en un operativo en el que también intervino una segunda embarcación de apoyo: nueve personas fueron detenidas y se incautaron casi seis toneladas de hachís. El herido fue la décima detención.

La violencia del narco en Huelva va en aumento: las incautaciones de hachís en la provincia se duplicaron hasta las 43 toneladas en 2025, según los datos del CITCO que recoge El País, y en junio otro grupo disparó con armas largas contra la Guardia Civil durante una descarga frustrada en la ría de Punta Umbría.

articles.headline: Diez años sin Diana Quer: el crimen que conmocionó a España y cambió la lucha contra los depredadores sexuales
articles.subtitle: El sábado se cumplió una década del asesinato de la joven de 18 años en A Pobra do Caramiñal; su padre y su hermana depositaron flores en su memoria y reivindicaron su legado.
articles.body:
Este sábado se cumplieron diez años del asesinato de Diana Quer, una de las tragedias que más conmocionó a España. Su padre, Juan Carlos Quer, y su hermana, Valeria, depositaron flores junto al monumento 'Como Auga', en los jardines Valle-Inclán de A Pobra do Caramiñal (A Coruña), donde la joven de 18 años desapareció en la madrugada del 22 de agosto de 2016, según informa El Progreso.

Juan Carlos Quer pidió honrar su memoria y recordó que 'su legado salvará vidas'. El padre de la joven se ha convertido desde entonces en un referente en la lucha contra la violencia machista, y el caso impulsó cambios legales, como la conocida como ley Diana Quer, que endureció las penas por el asesinato de mujeres.

José Enrique Abuín Gey, 'El Chicle', fue condenado por el crimen. RTVE recuerda estos días que el caso cambió la lucha contra los depredadores sexuales, y El Correo Gallego recoge el emotivo mensaje del padre en este décimo aniversario.

articles.headline: Newtownabbey stabbing: men arrested after man injured in Glenville Park attack
articles.subtitle: A 32-year-old man and a 58-year-old man were arrested after a man was stabbed in Newtownabbey on Saturday morning; both have since been released, one on bail, as police continue enquiries.
articles.body:
Two men have been arrested following a stabbing in Newtownabbey on Saturday morning. Police were called to Glenville Park at around 08:25 BST and found a man with injuries consistent with being stabbed; he was taken to hospital, where his injuries are not believed to be life-threatening.

A 32-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent and possession of an offensive weapon with intent, and a 58-year-old man on the same offences plus disorderly behaviour. Both have since been released — the 32-year-old on police bail and the 58-year-old unconditionally — as enquiries continue, the BBC reports.

Detective Inspector Hanbidge said the victim continues to receive treatment and appealed for anyone with dashcam or mobile phone footage to come forward. Police have urged witnesses to contact them. The Irish News reported that a man was airlifted to hospital following the incident.

articles.headline: Tributes paid to Eithne Vallely, 'giant of Irish traditional music', killed in Co Armagh crash
articles.subtitle: The 81-year-old co-founder of the Armagh Pipers Club died after being struck by a lorry on the Portadown Road on Friday morning; Sinn Féin MP Dáire Hughes led tributes.
articles.body:
Tributes have been paid to renowned traditional Irish musician Eithne Vallely after she died following a road crash in Co Armagh. The 81-year-old, originally from Co Donegal, was struck by a lorry in the Portadown Road area at around 8.20am on Friday and was pronounced dead at the scene, the PSNI said.

Ms Vallely co-founded the Armagh Pipers Club with her husband Brian, and the club said 'Eithne brought music into the lives of children for six decades'. Sinn Féin MP for Newry and Armagh Dáire Hughes described her as 'a giant of Irish cultural life', adding that her 'decades of contribution to music and cultural expression cannot be overstated'.

SDLP Armagh councillor Thomas O'Hanlon said that although she came from Donegal, 'she made Armagh her home', paying tribute to 'the thousands of people who learned to sing, to play and to love traditional music because of her influence'. Det Insp Stewart, of the PSNI's collision investigation unit, said the Portadown Road, which was closed for a time, has fully reopened.

articles.headline: Funeral of Derry fire victim Noel Rodgers to take place on Monday in Galliagh
articles.subtitle: The man in his 60s, who died after a fire at his flat in Bloomfield Park on Wednesday, will be remembered at 10am Requiem Mass in St Joseph's Church, with burial in the City Cemetery.
articles.body:
The funeral of Derry fire victim Noel Rodgers will take place on Monday morning. A Requiem Mass will be held at 10am in St Joseph's Church, Galliagh, with burial afterwards in the City Cemetery, the Derry Journal reports.

Mr Rodgers, who was in his 60s, died following a fire at his flat in Bloomfield Park on Wednesday afternoon. Foyle MP Colum Eastwood said he was shocked and saddened by his death, while Sinn Féin councillor Sandra Duffy described him as a lovely man who will be greatly missed by his family and the Galliagh community.

The Northern Ireland Fire and Rescue Service was called to the blaze on Wednesday afternoon, and the PSNI is continuing its enquiries into the circumstances of the fire.

articles.headline: Former detective reveals young female officers were 'stamped' in RUC initiation ceremony
articles.subtitle: The ex-officer, who joined in the early 1990s, said an official police stamper was used to 'brand' newly qualified female officers, an act she described as a sexual assault; Linzi McLaren has called for an investigation.
articles.body:
A former detective has revealed how young female officers were 'stamped' on the buttocks as part of an 'initiation ceremony' in the RUC. The former officer, who joined the force in the early 1990s and was posted to east Belfast, said the official police stamper was used to brand newly qualified female officers, an act she described as a sexual assault.

The revelations were published by The Irish News, which also reported that former PSNI officer Linzi McLaren, who joined in 2004, has called on Chief Constable Jon Boutcher to acknowledge the abuse and have it investigated: 'Station stamping should be investigated', she said.

The story comes days after Boutcher told the Policing Board that 17% of officers who took part in an internal survey said they had experienced inappropriate behaviour, with 14% saying they had witnessed it and 4.6% identifying misogyny, and after a review of the Katie Simpson case exposed systematic failures in policing and safeguarding.

articles.headline: French civil servant accused of drugging women in job interviews as investigation grows
articles.subtitle: BBC Global Women spoke to new accusers of Christian Nègre, the former culture ministry official alleged to have given diuretics to women in interviews; almost 250 women have come forward.
articles.body:
A BBC Global Women investigation has heard new allegations against Christian Nègre, the former senior civil servant accused of drugging women who came to him for job interviews at France's Ministry of Culture. Almost 250 women have alleged they were given diuretics during interviews, leaving them vulnerable to assault.

The BBC spoke to new accusers who described being chemically subdued during interviews that took place over several years, in a case that has drawn comparisons with the Gisèle Pelicot trial. The Guardian reported last November that women had alleged drugging by the senior official, who has denied the allegations.

The investigation against Nègre, who was suspended, remains open, and a trial date has yet to be set. Campaigners say the case has highlighted how diuretics can be used in chemical submission and have called for greater awareness among doctors and pharmacists.

articles.headline: Seven people killed in wrong-way crash between police car and car carrying five teenagers
articles.subtitle: Two police officers and five young people died in a head-on collision on the A66 near Middlesbrough on Saturday morning; police have said a pursuit was aborted seconds before the crash.
articles.body:
Seven people have died after a marked police car and a VW Passat carrying five teenagers collided head-on on the A66 near Middlesbrough in the early hours of Saturday. The two police officers and the five people in the Passat were pronounced dead at the scene, the BBC reported.

Police said officers had begun a pursuit after sighting a suspicious vehicle, but the pursuit was aborted seconds before the crash, The Irish Times reported on Sunday. Earlier reports suggested the Passat was travelling the wrong way, and police have said they are investigating the circumstances around the collision.

The A66 remained closed for much of Saturday as investigators worked at the scene, and the case has been referred to the police watchdog. Tributes have been paid to the officers and to the five young people killed, in an incident that has prompted renewed debate about police pursuit policies.

articles.headline: Gaza families search for missing detainees as Red Cross says more than 5,000 unaccounted for
articles.subtitle: Ten months after the ceasefire, families say relatives detained by Israel have simply vanished; the Red Cross has no access to prison records and Israel's prison service says it has no record of them.
articles.body:
Ten months after the ceasefire came into effect in Gaza, families say they still do not know what happened to loved ones detained by Israeli forces, and the Red Cross says more than 5,000 people remain missing.

In a BBC Global Women investigation, Id al-Drimli showed a picture of her son Mahmoud, who disappeared in 2024; this summer a photo emerged of two Israeli soldiers posing with a blindfolded prisoner that the family believes is him. The Israeli prison service said it had no record of holding him, and the military declined to comment.

Tal Steiner, an Israeli lawyer who helps locate Palestinians held by Israel, described the uncertainty as 'an open wound that doesn't heal'. The Hamas-run health ministry says more than 73,000 people have been killed in the war, and BBC reporting has detailed how Gaza doctors are investigating signs of torture on bodies returned to the territory.

articles.headline: First Android malware for car head units turns infotainment systems into proxy bots
articles.subtitle: Kaspersky found a dropper distributed via a fake update app to DoFun head units, using an MQTT server for instructions and a reverse-proxy module that commits ad fraud.
articles.body:
Security researchers at Kaspersky have documented what they describe as the first Android malware designed specifically for car infotainment systems. The malicious code, discovered in June, targets DoFun head units and is delivered through a trojanized update application called TWCore, which communicates with a command server over MQTT.

Once installed, the malware deploys a dropper (JarService) and a reverse-proxy module called zhima that turns the vehicle's head unit into part of a proxy botnet used for ad fraud. Kaspersky says the malware does not interfere with driving functions, but warns that a compromised infotainment system could be used to spy on users or as a gateway into other vehicle systems.

The vendor, DoFun, has been notified and says the issue has been fixed. BleepingComputer and The Hacker News reported the findings, with researchers recommending that owners update head units only through official channels and avoid third-party app stores.

articles.headline: Nonprofits say Microsoft sunset left 170,000 organizations without their data
articles.subtitle: Slate reports that organizations which relied on a retired Microsoft 365 offer lost OneDrive files when renewals lapsed; Microsoft says customers were warned to move their data before the program ended.
articles.body:
A Slate investigation has reported that some 171,000 nonprofits may have lost data stored on OneDrive after Microsoft retired a free Microsoft 365 offer for the sector. Organizations told the outlet they lost everything when their accounts lapsed at renewal, with one administrator describing how support could not restore the deleted files.

Microsoft says it emailed affected customers to warn them to move their data before the program ended, a claim several nonprofits dispute. The German site IT-Connect noted that the affected organizations were told their data would be deleted after the free offer was discontinued, with some reporting that even paid plans did not recover the files.

The story drew sharp criticism on Hacker News, where commenters questioned Microsoft's handling of the nonprofit program, and echoed a separate widely shared report of a 50-year-old Microsoft archive that was deleted early. Microsoft has said it is reviewing the cases reported.

articles.headline: Bun 1.4 ships: the JavaScript runtime's Rust rewrite reaches a stable release
articles.subtitle: The first stable release since the rewrite adds Bun.Image, Bun.WebView, Bun.cron and Bun.markdown, passes 1,517 more Node.js tests and cuts memory use and startup time.
articles.body:
Bun 1.4, the first stable release of the JavaScript runtime since its long-awaited rewrite in Rust, has shipped. The release adds more than 2,900 bug fixes, passes an additional 1,517 Node.js conformance tests, and delivers faster startup — 50% faster on Linux — with 35% lower memory use, according to the release notes.

New built-ins include Bun.Image, Bun.WebView, Bun.markdown, Bun.cron and Bun.Terminal, alongside new commands such as bun run --parallel, bun test --parallel, bun audit fix, bun dedupe and bun prune.

The decision to rewrite Bun in Rust was not without controversy: several contributors left the project over concerns about how the rewrite was handled, a debate that played out publicly on Hacker News and was covered by daily.dev. Bun's maintainers say the rewrite was necessary to fix deep-rooted issues in the original codebase.

articles.headline: Anthropic's best AI model struggles to attract users as cheaper tools thrive
articles.subtitle: The FT reports that corporate spending on Fable 5 has plateaued at around 11% of spending on Anthropic's tools, with customers shifting to cheaper Anthropic, OpenAI and open-weight models.
articles.body:
Anthropic's flagship model, Fable 5, is struggling to attract corporate users, with spending on the model plateauing at around 11% of what enterprises spend on Anthropic's tools, according to the Financial Times. Customers are increasingly choosing cheaper Anthropic models, OpenAI models or open-weight alternatives for everyday workloads.

The plateau comes just months after the model's launch and reflects growing price competition in the frontier AI market. Anthropic's overall business continues to grow — July revenue was an annualized $65bn, with 6,000 customers spending more than $100,000 a year — but the company is now positioning cheaper tiers as its main growth driver.

Anthropic has also begun embedding Claude Mythos 5 in its security products and pledged $35m in compute credits as it courts enterprises. The FT's reporting was widely discussed on Hacker News.

articles.headline: ChatGPT search now uses the site: operator at scale, data shows
articles.subtitle: Simon Willison flags that ChatGPT search now applies the site: operator at scale, letting users restrict results to a specific domain; Promptwatch data shows a surge in usage of the operator.
articles.body:
Simon Willison has flagged a change in how ChatGPT search works: it now applies the site: operator at scale, letting users restrict results to a specific domain. Willison says the change makes ChatGPT search genuinely more useful for site-specific lookups, and notes that it follows OpenAI's recent improvements to GPT-5.6.

Data from Promptwatch shows the site: operator now accounts for a significant share of ChatGPT search queries, with a surge in usage since the change rolled out. OpenAI says the update is part of ongoing work to improve search quality.

For publishers and developers, the shift matters: reliably restricting a search to one site changes how the tool can be used for research, fact-checking and SEO monitoring, and Promptwatch's analysis breaks down the fan-out costs involved in serving the operator at scale.
